audit.whatIsWrong: Kled's chart gave Levels 3 and 4-5 to Skill and Levels 6 and First item to Dr. Mundo. The already-audited mirror set Mundo's page to 'Kled wins Level 1 through First item; Dr. Mundo takes 2+ items, ratings 3/4/4/4/5/5/7', so the two pages currently answer 'who wins Level 6' differently.
audit.why: 56.16% over 292 games with Mundo as one of the weakest early laners; Kled's percent-health Bear Trap scales against exactly the health he stacks. The mirror's ratings invert to 7/6/6/6/5/5/3 on Kled's side.
audit.corrected: Levels 3, 4-5, 6 and First item flipped to Kled in both layers; ratings set to the mirror-inverse 6/10, 6/10, 5/10, 5/10. whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten so they no longer call those stages even.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere; packet reports zero sequencing cues.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank — a 120s ultimate is a whole wave of freedom if you bait it. Infected Bonesaw is only 4s at 975 range, so it is not a trackable window and step-ups must be keyed to Heart Zapper instead.
audit.corrected: 17s in dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns; 120s in whys[4]; the 4s/975 range in dontsFull[2].d so the reader stops treating cleaver dodging as a plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup was absent from the entire page: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits Mundo. Kled's whole pattern opens with Bear Trap on a Rope's hook and yank — which that passive simply eats. Also missing: Heart Zapper heals off a share of the damage STORED from what you deal into it, so trading into it actively pays him.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby.' Riot's W text: 'storing a portion of damage he takes... he heals a percentage of the stored damage.' Together they mean the correct sequence is: spend a cheap Bear Trap to strip the passive, wait out Heart Zapper's 17s, then commit — not open with the pin. Blunt Force Trauma is also an auto-reset that scales off his MISSING health, so it hits hardest exactly when you think you are winning.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and wants.foe[0] state the passive eating your first immobilise; dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d and report[5].t state Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal; dontsFull[1].d states Blunt Force Trauma scaling off his missing health; whys[4] keys the commit to the passive being spent.

notes: Chart set to the mirror's prescription (Kled through First item, Mundo at 2+ items, ratings 7/6/6/6/5/5/3) rather than to the packet chart, which had Skill at three of those rows — the mirror's page is already live on Mundo's side and the two must not disagree. The buried mechanic worth the whole audit: Goes Where He Pleases resists Mundo's first immobilizing effect, so Kled's opening Bear Trap hook is absorbed and dropped as a cannister he can walk over to heal. Nothing on the page said this. Infected Bonesaw scales off the target's CURRENT health, not max health, which is why it is a poke tool rather than an execute.
